query:
Which supplied authorities help analyze the live Delhi DRC1958s14(1)(b) issue shown by this allowed record, respecting the target procedural stage, rival assertions and scope limits? Do not predict the withheld target verdict.
 This is an application under clause (a) and (b) of the proviso to sub-section (1) of cite10†section 14 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act 59 of 1958') made by applicant against respondents for recovery of possession of premises i.e. shop bearing No. 1897, Main Bazar, Chandni Chowk, Delhi-110006 more specifically shown red in the site plan annexed with the application.
2. It is stated in the application that that the petitioner is the landlord of the premises No. 1897, Main Bazar, Chandni Chowk, Delhi which was that out for commercial purposes to the respondent at the monthly rent of Rs. 550/- per month. That the respondents have failed to pay or tender the rent w.e.f. 1.8.2002 at the rate of Rs.
500/- per month within two months of the services of the notice of demand dated 4.8.2007 alongwith interest and after the expiry of 3 days from the service of the notice under cite11†Section 6-A of the DRC Act at the rate of Rs.550/- per month w.e.f. 1.7.2007 onwards. The respondent has sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the premises under the tenancy of the respondent to a Wine merchant and wine and bear shop is being run in the premises in dispute.
The said sub-letting, assigning or parting with the possession of the suit premises has been done by the respondents without obtaining the consent in writing of the petitioner after 9th day of June, 1952. Notice dated 4.6.2007 was served upon the respondents. A reply to the notice dated 11.6.2007 was received. The copy of the original notice, and original reply is enclosed herewith.
The premises in dispute is situated E-559/14/11 2/14 in an area declared to be slum area and necessary permission from the Competent Authority, Slum has been obtained vide order dated 10.3.2010. Bank A/c No of petitioner is SB A/C No. 26657, Bank Of India, Hamdard Branch Lal Kuan, Delhi. It is, therefore, prayed that an eviction order in respect of the premises in dispute i.e. shop bearing No.
1897, Main Bazar, Chandni Chowk, Delhi-110006 more specifically shown red in the annexed plan, may be passed in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents with cost of the present petition.
3. The application of eviction is contested by the respondents by way of a written statement of defence. That the petition as filed by the petitioner is without any cause of action and hence the same is liable to be dismissed under order VII Rule 11 of the code of Civil Procedure. That the present petition has been filed without any just cause and reasons and the same is a gross mis-use of the legal process of law and hence the same is not maintainable in the eyes of the law.
It is mis-conceived and has been filed just to humiliate and harass the answering respondents. The allegations made in the petition are vexatious and meritless and dies not disclose the clear right to sue and hence, the same is liable to be dismissed. That the petition has been filed just to harass he answering respondents as the answering respondents are in legal possession of the suit property for the last more than 50 years.
That the petition is not maintainable at all which is totally based on wrong, false and incorrect information. That the present petition is not maintainable in view of the fact that the respondents have not sub-letted the suit property to the DTDC and the respondent is E-559/14/11 3/14 gaining commission from the sale and purchase of the liquor from the suit property and the relationship of the respondent and the DTDC is merely a lessor and lessee.
It is specifically denied that the respondents have failed to pay or tender the rent w.e.f. 1.8.2002 at the rate of Rs. 500/- per month within two months of the services of notice of demand dt. 4.8.2007 alongwith interest as alleged. It is submitted that earlier Smt.
Zubida Khatoon was owner and landlady of the tenanted premises and the rent was paid by the respondents to her and thereafter the father of the petitioner claimed himself owner of the tenanted premises and started accepting the rent from the respondents, which was regularly paid to him through cheques. After his death, the petitioner started claiming to be the only owner of the tenanted premises.
The respondents requested to the petitioner to give the details and particulars of all the legal heirs of the deceased Shikh Mohd. Yusuf but the petitioner avoided to give the same to the respondents despite repeated requests made by the respondents with the petitioner. The respondents sent a cheque of rent amounting to Rs.
8000/- (Rupees eight thousand only) upto July, 2002 with the condition for encashing the said cheque only after the necessary information alongwith the documents regarding the legal heirs of the deceased Sheikh Mohd. Yusuf were furnished by the petitioner to the respondent but with malafide intention, the petitioners encashed the said cheque. However, till date, no particulars and details of the legal heirs of deceased Sheikh Mohd. Yusuf have been furnished by the petitioners to the respondent.
Therefore the intention of the petitioner is malafide. It is further submitted that till the E-559/14/11 4/14 petitioner provides the complete information regarding the other legal heirs of the deceased Sheikh Mohd. Yusuf alongwith other documentary proof, the petitioner is not entitled to claim the rent from the respondent.
It is denied that the respondent has sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the premises under the tenancy of the respondent to a Wine Merchant or Wine or bear shop is being run in the premises in dispute as alleged. It is denied that the said sub-letting, assigning or parting with the possession of the suit premises has been done by the respondents without obtaining the consent in writing of the petitioner after 9th of June, 1952 as alleged.
It is submitted that the wine or bear shop is being run in the tenanted shop since 1985 on license basis given by the respondents without paying of rent with the permission of deceased landlord Sheikh Mohd. Yusuf , who was duly informed by the respondents in this regard and that is why during the life-time, he never protested or initiated any legal action against the respondents in this regard. Hence, all the allegations made in the para under reply regarding the alleged sub- letting etc.
are not only false but the allegations made are motivated and have been leveled with malafide intention and ulterior motives by the petitioner in order to create false eviction ground against the respondents. Even otherwise, it is submitted that the legal possession of the tenanted premises is with the respondents.
It is submitted that the shop in question is under the possession of wine shop by virtue of License Deed executed between DTTDC and the respondents and it has been agreed by the DTTDC to pay the monthly commission on the sale of liquor in the shop E-559/14/11 5/14 and not rent as fixed or either paid by DTTDC. The agreement is license and not a lease.
The legal possession of the shop is with the respondent and DTTDC is only a licensee and is being permitted to use the shop for selling the wine as stated above, and hence, therefore, there is no question of Sub-letting, assigning or parting with the possession of the shop by the respondents to the wine shop as alleged by the petitioner. The allegations made in this regard are mis-conceived and not sustainable in the eyes of law.
It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to dismiss the petition of the petitioner with costs and special compensatory costs as provided under cite12†section 35-A of the CPC.
4. A replication has been filed by the applicant to the written statement of the respondents wherein the averments made in the application for eviction have been reiterated whereas the defence taken by the respondents in their written statement are traversed.
5. After completion of pleadings and hearing counsel for the parties concerned an order under cite13†section 15(1) of Act 59 of 1958 was passed whereby the respondents were directed to clear the arrears of rent and further directed to pay or deposit the monthly rent month by month.
6. In support of his case, the applicant got examined himself as PW-1 Sheikh Mohd. Iqbal and during his examination in chief tendered his affidavit Ex.PW1/A alongwith documents Ex.PW-1 to Ex.PW-1 and Ex.PW-7 and he was duly cross-examined by counsel for the respondents and thereafter, evidence on behalf of the applicant was closed.
7. In support of their case the respondents got examined RW1 E-559/14/11 6/14 Mr. Anil Kalra who during his examination in chief tendered his affidavit Ex.RW1/A alongwith document Ex.RW1/1 and he was cross-examined by counsel for the applicant. The respondents also got examined RW-2 summoned witness from DTTDC and this witness was also cross- examined by the counsel for the petitioner. Thereafter, evidence on behalf of the respondents was closed.
